evidence.snippet: - **The gate takes the worst standing round.** Two rounds that stand together, because two hosts reviewed at once, gate by the worse, and not reviewed is worse than blocking.

- The gate is a command, `melian gate "#N"`. It lists the record, computes the verdict of each standing round for the pull request's base and head, and exits with the worst. Any provider's CI can run it. The merge-group check runs it and writes the group's status; a status on the head is a display, and no gate reads one. Just before it writes that status, or copies an override, the check lists again, and computes again when the set differs from the one it read, as [the coordination decision](2026-11-08-how-melian-coordinates.md) requires of any job that writes from an authority it read earlier.

verification.reason: The new RecordGate.decide (record-gate.ts 143-153) unions each exact-revision round's covered checks into one `covered` set. coverage() (264-270) returns only checks in `reviewed.ran`, or skipped checks the tier allows. reviewed() returns a Verdict, not a refusal, when a check failed, so a failed guardrails or lens check is simply left out of A's coverage. Round B at the same revision covers it, so `gaps` is empty and `failures` is empty. With no live findings, #merged gives status `passed` and passes() is true. Every round at one revision stands, because the head's own plan leaves `replaces` empty. The base decision (shared-record-behind-a-store-port, rule 4, line 119) says 'The gate takes the worst standing round... not reviewed is worse than blocking', and line 203 says the gate 'exits with the worst'. The head computes a per-check union instead, so a standing not-reviewed round A no longer fails the gate. The only text supporting the union is head-added (cli.md line 21 and the plan), and head text cannot excuse the departure. The base reason, that two hosts reviewing at once gate by the worse, still holds. The coverage-ledger 'series of reviews' ruling concerns delta rounds at different heads, not two standing rounds of one revision. Findings are still merged strictest-first, so the weakening is limited to the not-reviewed status (failed or limit-hit checks), which is the case the claim names.

evidence.snippet: signed: "carries a signature, and no repository key exists to check one",

- One that takes pull requests from forks, whatever `trust.writers` says, because without the key the gate cannot tell the trusted host's record of a fork's head from a writer's. For a fork's head the gate counts only records that key signed, so a repository that has not pinned it passes no fork's pull request, and the gate names what to set up. The maintainer ruled so on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session, over the alternative of a writer's recorded vouch: the rule's promise is that a fork's head was reviewed where its code could not touch the result, and a vouch promises only that a writer read it.

  This changes one clause of the coverage ledger decision's "Fork heads" section, which said no round of a fork's head records coverage, whoever runs it. A round the trusted host ran and signed now does. That section already named this end: in milestone 3 the agent refuses a record "whose head is not a writer's or the App's", and the trusted host is that App. The rest of the section stands. A writer's round of a fork's head records no coverage and reads not reviewed, with `--trust-head` or without it, because a writer's machine ran the fork's code where it could touch the result. A record of a fork's head with no signature, a bad one, or one from a key the base does not pin covers nothing. A repository with no pinned key passes no fork's pull request.

verification.reason: gate.ts is new in this change. It only checks that the base tip sets trust.writers, then calls RecordGate.decide with everyRecordCounts. Neither the gate nor RecordGate reads the head's repository or the writer's trust (searching record-gate.ts for writer/trust returns nothing). Nothing else in the gate path separates a fork's head either. Searches of packages/pipeline/src and packages/cli/src find fork handling only in the relay, the check hand-over and the header-level kind filter. The only writer-trust code is writerTrust in commands.ts and relay.ts, and it never reaches the gate. The review side also records no "no coverage for a fork's head". review.ts uses `writer` only for probe and mutation permission, and "coverage is not recorded for a fork's head" appears nowhere in packages. So a writer's `--trust-head` round of a fork's head exports ordinary covering records. If a writer adds them to melian/state, the gate counts them and can exit 0. The base decision (rule 6, lines 172-174) says that for a fork's head the gate counts only records signed by the pinned host key, and that a writer's round of a fork's head covers nothing, with or without `--trust-head`. The repository has no key check at all (record-relay.ts line 73 says "no repository key exists to check one"). A fork's pull request therefore passes on a writer's unsigned round, where the decision says it passes nothing. I did not run this end to end, but each step is traced in code. The scenario needs a writer to push the records, which narrows who can trigger it but not the weakened rule.

evidence.snippet: - An unresolved acknowledge finding fails the gate, as a blocking finding does and as [the acknowledge status rule](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md) has it for a host's publication. A writer resolves one by recording the read as a dismissal with its reason, from any host, since a dismissal now reaches the record. [The Actions round's status](2026-11-07-actions-round-sets-melian-review.md) exempted an Actions round because a runner could not dismiss; that reason is gone, and so is the exemption once the gate is the required check. The maintainer ruled so on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session. Until then the Actions status keeps its own rule, as a display.

This excludes members lifted only from silent to advisory under “Pre-existing, important”.
  An opted-in pre-existing acknowledgement counts, new or carried. Dismissed and refuted findings do not.

verification.reason: Traced: RecordedRound.findingsUnder runs the round's findings through Adjudication under the base tip's policy. An opted-in pre-existing P1 therefore resolves to `acknowledge` and sits in verdict.findings.acknowledge. RecordGate.#merged then keeps only findings where `proves` is true. `proves` needs the finding's path, or its trigger or proof file, to be among revision.paths(). A pre-existing finding is outside the diff and has no trigger, so `proves` is false and the finding never enters `live`. findings.acknowledge ends up empty, and passes() requires only block + acknowledge === 0 and a status other than not-reviewed, so the gate passes. The decision it cites, rule 9 (line 204) of the shared-record decision, says an unresolved acknowledge finding fails the gate as the acknowledge status rule does for publication. That rule (acknowledge-status-exact-rule, lines 28-29) says an opted-in pre-existing acknowledgement counts. The gate therefore drops a class the rule says must fail it. The head's own comments and progress log state the diff filter as intended, but the base rule's reason still holds. No test I could find covers a pre-existing acknowledgement off the diff. The filter does make sense for rounds whose base differs from the merge's, but for an exact-diff round it fails open.
